name: Attleboro
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Attleboro, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Attleboro, MA: La Salette's million-light Festival of Lights, the Holiday Happening parade and the Capron Park Zoo tree lighting.
lede: Attleboro lights more than one million free Christmas lights at La Salette, sends a city parade to Highland Park for Santa and pony rides, and opens Capron Park Zoo after dark to light a 60-foot tree.
celebrates: The season in Attleboro runs on three big traditions. The National Shrine of Our Lady of La Salette on Park Street turns on more than one million lights every night from late November into January, with free entry, Santa on weekend nights, a carousel and a hayride. The City of Attleboro Parks and Forestry Department sends its Holiday Happening parade from Brennan Middle School to Highland Park for a free family festival with Santa, pony rides and tractor hayrides. Capron Park Zoo opens after hours on Small Business Saturday for Miracle on County Street, lighting its 60-foot tree among the animals.
lastyear: In 2025 the city held its Holiday Happening and Parade on Saturday, December 6, from 10 am to 2 pm at Highland Park, and the city says the day drew more than 1,000 people. La Salette's Festival of Lights ran nightly through the holidays, and Capron Park Zoo held its third Miracle on County Street tree lighting with a toy drive for the Greater Attleboro Area Council for Children's Christmas is for Kids program.
facts: Attleboro was part of Rehoboth until it became its own town in 1694, and it became the City of Attleboro in 1914, dropping the ugh that North Attleborough kept. Many early settlers came from Attleborough, England, which gave the city its name. Attleboro was once known as the Jewelry Capital of the World for its many jewelry makers. La Salette's International Creche Museum holds about 2,000 nativity scenes from more than 100 countries.
trains: Attleboro sits on the MBTA Providence/Stoughton Line, and the Attleboro commuter rail station is in the downtown area, so a ride from Boston's South Station can be part of a holiday day out. For a train ride with Christmas lights, Edaville in Carver runs its holiday train through the season. The Old Colony and Fall River Railroad Museum in Fall River is a short drive east, and the Boston Street Railway Association keeps Boston-area trolley history alive.

traditions: La Salette Christmas Festival of Lights
The National Shrine of Our Lady of La Salette lights more than one million lights every night from 5 to 9 pm, with free entry.
The city's parade runs from Brennan Middle School to Highland Park for a free festival with Santa, pony rides and hayrides.
Capron Park Zoo opens after hours to light its 60-foot tree, with carolers, food trucks, vendors and Santa.
Holiday Toy Drive at the zoo
Families bring new, unwrapped toys to the tree lighting for the Christmas is for Kids program.
La Salette's museum shows about 2,000 nativity scenes from more than 100 countries, free to visit.
kidfact: La Salette uses more than one million lights for its Christmas festival. If you counted one light every second without stopping, it would take you more than 11 days to count them all.
faq: Yes. Entry to the Christmas Festival of Lights at the National Shrine of Our Lady of La Salette is free, and the shrine welcomes free-will donations. The lights are on every night from 5 to 9 pm, even on Christmas night. Santa photos, the carousel, the hayride and the Ride to Bethlehem run on Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights.
When is the Attleboro Christmas parade?

The Holiday Happening parade is held on a Saturday morning in early December. It leaves Brennan Middle School, travels Rathbun-Willard Drive and Dennis Street, and ends at Highland Park, where the City of Attleboro Parks and Forestry Department holds a free festival with Santa, pony rides, tractor hayrides, crafts and live music until 2 pm.
Does Capron Park Zoo do anything for Christmas?

Yes. On Small Business Saturday the zoo opens after hours for Miracle on County Street, its holiday tree lighting. Families see animals after dark, hear carolers, visit food trucks and local vendors, take a photo with Santa and watch the 60-foot tree light up. Tickets are sold online through SimpleTix.
When is the best time to see the La Salette lights?

The shrine suggests coming on a weeknight. Traffic builds 30 minutes to an hour before the lights come on at 5 pm, and on weekends close to Christmas it can stretch a quarter mile in each direction. Everything closes at 9 pm, and the shrine recommends a small flashlight for the parking lot.
Can we take the train to Attleboro?

Yes. The MBTA Providence/Stoughton Line stops at the Attleboro commuter rail station, with trains to and from Boston's South Station. From the station, families can continue to La Salette, Highland Park or Capron Park Zoo by car, taxi or rideshare.
